questions: Has the split or double appearance of the uvula been present since childhood?
Have you ever had difficulty swallowing, nasal regurgitation of food or liquids, or unusually nasal speech?
Do you have recurrent sore throats or episodes of uvular swelling?
Have you had any recent surgery, endoscopy, dental procedure, or placement of a breathing tube?
Have you recently injured, bitten, or burned the back of your mouth or throat?
Have you noticed bleeding, pain, or a change in the uvula since it first appeared split?
Do you hear or feel a rhythmic clicking in either ear?
Have you had double vision, difficulty coordinating movements, weakness, numbness, or trouble walking?
Have you had a stroke, head injury, brain infection, or other neurological illness?
orders: Perform a bedside oropharyngeal examination with a tongue depressor, including inspection and gentle palpation of the soft palate and uvula, assessment of uvular elevation during “ah,” and assessment for a midline palatal defect or mass.
MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium, including thin-section images of the brainstem and cerebellum, to evaluate for lesions causing symptomatic palatal tremor.
